unit.why: A short anecdote about the Maggid of Mezeritch, who could not afford the costly Etz Hayyim and hired himself out as a teacher for a term to buy it.

stories.start_quote: עוד שמעתי ממנו שסיפר שהרה״מ הי'
stories.end_quote: דמי השכירות את ספה"ק עץ החיים
stories.summary_en: The Maggid longed to own the rare and costly Etz Hayyim of the Ari, so he hired himself out as a melamed for a term and spent his entire wages on the book.

quotes: הספה"ק עץ החיים מהאר״י הקדוש ז"ל
tags.why: The object of his longing is the central Lurianic kabbalistic work.

quotes: כי הי' אז מחירו רב מחמת יוקר מציאותו
וקנה בעד כל דמי השכירות את ספה"ק עץ החיים
tags.why: He acquires a rare kabbalistic book; it is a printed book rather than a hidden manuscript.
The anecdote shows his devotion and self-sacrifice for kabbalistic learning.

quotes: הי' משתוקק מאד לקנות לו הספה"ק עץ החיים
tags.why: His desire to study Lurianic kabbalah is implied, but study itself is not depicted.
The story is framed as one told by an informant.

missing_concepts: working as a melamed (teacher) for wages
sacrifice to acquire holy books / the high price of books
